purpose: Read-only map from research ideas to actual production code. These are not full reproductions of the papers.

items.title: MemGPT: bounded context and external memory
items.status: Inspired by the memory-tier idea; not a full MemGPT implementation.
items.explain: The backend keeps selected recent messages and older evidence within a finite prompt allowance. It does not implement model-controlled paging or the full MemGPT operating-system abstraction.
items.limit: The input estimator is a conservative UTF-8 byte bound, not exact tokenizer counting. There is no universal 70-percent paging rule here.

items.title: RAG: retrieve source text before generation
items.status: A local retrieval-augmented pipeline; not the original jointly trained RAG model.
items.explain: Nomic embeds text, Chroma compares query and stored vectors, and Python sends the selected original words to Qwen. Qwen never reads Nomic vectors directly.
items.limit: Similarity is relevance, not correctness. A fetched candidate can be excluded by the cutoff or already included through recent history.

items.title: Summary memory: bounded older excerpts
items.status: Our extractive summary baseline. Not a complete published memory system.
items.explain: Older learner excerpts are selected under a byte budget, while recent turns stay separate. Source IDs and a source-content signature support refresh after edits.
items.limit: This copies and truncates source excerpts. Asking Qwen to summarize the chat is a different operation. It may omit important older facts.

items.title: Mem0 connection: updating and removing remembered information
items.status: Our mutation implementation addresses a related design concern; it does not reproduce Mem0 extraction/consolidation.
items.explain: Supported corrections and forgetting requests trigger backend operations on source and derived records. The model saying it forgot is not sufficient.
items.limit: The database checks cover selected mutation paths in isolated namespaces. They do not prove arbitrary natural-language deletion or all concurrency cases. We do not have separately retained facts surviving the current whole-session inactivity expiry.

items.title: A-MEM connection: linked memories and source evidence
items.status: A restricted rule-based Neo4j implementation; not full A-MEM agentic memory evolution.
items.explain: Learner assertions, topics and source messages are linked. Supported later statements can deactivate old facts, and the retrieval path returns textual evidence.
items.limit: Neo4j is our implementation choice, not a requirement of A-MEM. We do not implement unrestricted self-organizing notes, general inference, or permanent fact retention. Topic mentions alone are not learner facts.

items.title: LoCoMo: questions, predictions and upstream scoring
items.status: Our runner uses released data and downloaded upstream scoring functions.
items.explain: The runner loads source history, builds context, generates using local Qwen, then scores against held-out references. F1, adversarial abstention, context time and generation request time are separate measurements.
items.limit: 49 fixed questions x 4 modes x 3 trials = 588 predictions, not the full dataset. Upstream scorer code was downloaded, not invented by us. Re-scoring saved predictions is not a new model run.

items.title: Supporting application code: SQL, OCR, instructions and retention
items.status: Engineering support, not a claimed reproduction of a research paper.
items.explain: JSON stores working records, MySQL keeps recoverable persistence, response blueprints supply instructions, and Tesseract supplies image text. Session expiry is a separate retention policy.
items.limit: OCR extracts text rather than visual reasoning. Qwen reads instructions inserted by Python, not JSON files directly. The current timer expires tracked whole sessions after one hour of inactivity.
